reading: The grid is cut into panels by full separator lines; two rows and two columns of separator colour have panel-colour gaps where they cross each other. Output is the box spanned by those four gap cells, outline included.

new_rows.name: gapc
new_rows.datalog:
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowc(Y, C, count(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
sepc(C) :- rowc(Y, C, N), maxx(M), N = M + 1.
gapc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, D), !sepc(D), sepc(C), Y1 = Y - 1, Y2 = Y + 1, X1 = X - 1, X2 = X + 1, px(Y1, X, C), px(Y2, X, C), px(Y, X1, C), px(Y, X2, C).

why: exactly four non-separator cells have separator colour on all 4 sides; their bounding box equals the output
invariants: output cells are copied unchanged from the input

reading: The 8 shape moves down one row and is recoloured 2.
why: output shape = input shape translated by (+1,0), colour 8 -> 2

reading: Each 5x5 box outlined by 0 has a 3x3 interior; every 0 interior cell (except the centre) is written with a fixed keypad digit for its position: 1 7 6 / 4 . 5 / 2 9 3. Interior 8 cells and the centre stay.

slots.boxes: 5x5 regions whose border ring is all 0
slots.subject: 0 cells of each box interior, centre excluded

why: for each interior position the 0->digit value is the same in every box of every pair; 8 cells never change

reading: Each row has one 5; the whole row is painted by the 5's column: column 0 -> 2, column 1 -> 4, column 2 -> 3.

slots.key: column index of the row's 5 -> colour {0:2, 1:4, 2:3} (learned from train)

why: every output row is uniform with the colour keyed by the 5's position in that input row

reading: Nine 3x3 pieces (grey 5 with coloured edge/corner cells) are scattered on the input; they are assembled like a jigsaw into a 9x9 grey square, each piece placed where its coloured cells form the outer border pattern (corners at corners, edges at edge-middles, plain piece in the centre).

slots.slot: 3x3 position in output chosen by which sides of the piece carry colour

why: output is a 3x3 arrangement of the input pieces unchanged, coloured cells all on the outer ring

reading: All-0 rectangles at least 2x2 are filled with 2, except a rectangle overlapped by a strictly larger such rectangle (largest-first).
why: every 2 cell lies in a >=2x2 all-0 rectangle not overlapped by a larger one; all other cells unchanged (plain 2x2 cover over-fills 2 cells in pair 3)

reading: The single 2 is erased and replaced by four diagonal neighbours: 3 up-left, 6 up-right, 8 down-left, 7 down-right (clipped at the border).
why: output = constant 3x3 pattern [[3,0,6],[0,0,0],[8,0,7]] centred on the 2, cropped to the grid

reading: Inside the 5-walled cavity, the longest diagonal run of 0 cells that starts in a top pocket corner is recoloured 8.

new_rows.name: diag
new_rows.datalog:
dir(DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 1, DX > 0.
dir(DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 1, DX < 0.
start(Y, X, DX) :- dir(DX), px(Y, X, 0), Y1 = Y - 1, X1 = X - DX, !px(Y1, X, 0), !px(Y, X1, 0), !px(Y1, X1, 0).
ray(Y0, X0, DX, Y, X) :- start(Y0, X0, DX), Y = Y0, X = X0.
ray(Y0, X0, DX, Y2, X2) :- ray(Y0, X0, DX, Y, X), Y2 = Y + 1, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, 0).
len(Y0, X0, DX, count(Y, X)) :- ray(Y0, X0, DX, Y, X).
best(max(N)) :- len(Y0, X0, DX, N).
diag(Y, X) :- ray(Y0, X0, DX, Y, X), len(Y0, X0, DX, N), best(M), N = M.

why: the 8 cells are exactly one maximal diagonal 0-run, the longest among runs whose upper end has walls above and beside it (unique on every pair); key 0 -> 8

reading: Pairs of 2x2 blocks of 8 sit on the same two rows; the 2-row strip strictly between each pair is cut out, and the strips are stacked top to bottom.

slots.brackets: 2x2 solid 8 squares paired by shared rows
slots.region: cells strictly between the two squares of a pair (2 rows high)
slots.combine: stack strips vertically in row order

why: every output 2-row band equals the input strip between one 8-square pair; all pairs have equal gap width

reading: Count the 8-connected objects of each colour on the 7 background and draw a bottom-aligned bar chart: fixed columns 5,2,8,9,6, bar height = object count, height = max count, empty is 7.

slots.count: number of 8-connected single-colour objects per colour

why: each output column c is 7 above and colour c in its bottom count(c) cells on every pair
